packageRules.description: Group GitHub Actions major updates into a single PR so a batch of action majors arrives as one reviewable change rather than one PR per action.
Automerge patch and digest updates after required checks
Keep unstable dependencies under manual review

Major updates merge on green: the merge train's full suite is the gate, so a major no longer waits for a human. The rules below are the exceptions: js-yaml, fast-uri and postgres majors are disabled outright (enabled: false); pytest, Python, primevue/@primevue/themes and @primeuix/styled are capped with allowedVersions, so an out-of-range major is never proposed; and @sentry/vue, mcp and github-actions majors are held for manual review (automerge: false).
js-yaml v5 dropped YAML merge-key (<<) expansion — manifest tier/role gating depends on it

Hold fast-uri on the 3.x line. ajv@8.20.0 declares fast-uri ^3.0.1 and the frontend pnpm override caps it at >=3.1.9 <4; 3.1.9 already carries every published fast-uri advisory (GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp, GHSA-w74x-v6f9-j3xg, GHSA-wjr9-j795-jxcr, GHSA-xhq7-xmqj-769h), so a v4 bump adds no security benefit and would pin ajv outside its declared range. Remove once ajv itself accepts fast-uri 4.x.

Hold pytest below 9.2. pytest 9.2 renamed FixtureManager._arg2fixturedefs, which the pinned pytest-bdd commit (60f6625b) still reads, so all BDD scenarios fail with AttributeError. Keep backend/pyproject.toml's pytest constraint at >=9.1.1,<9.2.0 until a pytest-bdd release supports the rename. Remove this once the pytest-bdd pin is bumped to a compatible release.

Hold Python below 3.15. python:3.15-slim breaks the prod image build: zstandard 0.25.0 ships no cp315 wheel, so 'uv sync --frozen' falls back to an sdist build that needs gcc, which the images' --no-build policy forbids (see revert #1721). The same cap must apply to backend/pyproject.toml's requires-python (pep621) - the Dockerfile base image must sit inside its range per tests/architecture/test_fly_toml_python_version.py - so match both the docker base image and the python-version datasource. Remove this once the native dependencies publish cp315 wheels.

Hold actions/setup-python's python-version below 3.15 by manager. The datasource-scoped Hold Python rule above did not catch Renovate's github-actions extraction of the actions/setup-python 'with: python-version' input (PR #3548 bumped the Copy consistency job to 3.15), so cap it explicitly by manager. Remove together with the Hold Python rule once the native dependencies publish cp315 wheels.

Hold PrimeVue at v4. PrimeVue 5 cannot be packaged for self-hosters because of its licensing, so the stack was deliberately kept on PrimeVue 4 and these caps must not be raised without a licensing decision that supports self-hosted redistribution.

Hold @primeuix/styled below v1. PrimeVue 5 cannot be packaged for self-hosters because of its licensing, so the stack was deliberately kept on PrimeVue 4 and these caps must not be raised without a licensing decision that supports self-hosted redistribution. @primeuix/styled v1 ships with the PrimeVue 5 line, which is why it is capped below v1 even though it sits on 0.7.x today.

Hold postgres below a major bump. postgres:16-alpine is the image in deploy/compose/docker-compose.prod.yml as well as every test and CI database, so a major bump changes the production database image, not just CI. PostgreSQL 16 is the only supported runtime database (ADR 068), and a green run on a newer major does not validate 16. Expanding supported PostgreSQL versions is tracked in a separate ticket; until that lands this stays held.

Hold @sentry/vue major updates for manual review. Sentry fails silently, so a green build proves the least here; validation that the new major actually reports errors is tracked separately, and this hold comes off when it passes.

Hold mcp major updates for manual review. mcp is the MCP server SDK, where a protocol change can pass tests and still break tool calls at runtime; validation is tracked separately, so a human signs off on the major until then.

Hold GitHub Actions major updates for manual review. The 'GitHub Actions majors' grouping rule exists so a batch of action majors arrives as one reviewable change, not to merge unattended: a third-party action major carries supply-chain risk that a green build cannot fully validate (the same reasoning as the @sentry/vue and mcp holds), and exempting it from the global major-automerge rule is what keeps that grouping PR human-reviewed. This rule sits after the global major-automerge rule so its automerge:false wins.
